Subject: DRAFT — Please do not enter 43 or attempt propping

Mick, please don’t go into 43 at 9, with your lad or anyone else. Priya, please don’t hand over a key for this. No DIY propping and no loft inspection from inside.

I’m a chartered structural engineer with IStructE, but I’m writing as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement at about 7. This isn’t a commission or a structural inspection, and I have no professional indemnity cover for free advice. I cannot certify either house as safe.

What I could see was concerning: roughly 1.2 metres of chimney still standing at 41, leaning towards 43, with visibly deteriorated mortar at its base. At 43 there’s a substantial hole in the roof, a stepped crack above the bay and apparent downward movement at the bay head. These are visual estimates, not measurements.

Standing under that roof to install props would put you directly beneath possible falling masonry. Debris may be loading the floors, and we don’t know how loads are now being carried through the damaged building. Two props are not a safe answer without assessment.

Jo, your cousin’s point about terraces generally being robust is fair, but this one is damaged.

Priya, I would not treat the pavement as safe: loose slates are visible along the gutter line at 43 and 45. The tape only covers 43’s garden. Please use the opposite pavement, especially on the school run, pending council assessment and clearance. The council already knows, but please urgently update dangerous structures via the main council number, which also handles out-of-hours calls, about the unclosed footway and planned entry.

I can’t establish whether Mrs Doherty is safe. Although 45’s front looks undamaged, I couldn’t see the shared wall. It isn’t my decision, but I would not sleep in her front room tonight; staying with family until 45 is checked would be preferable.
